question: Before battling Second Sister (二姐), the player and Bajie transform into two pig demons, one big and one small. Which pig demon does the player transform into?

rollouts.answer: The player transforms into the larger pig demon; Bajie is the smaller one. The larger pig dissolves in red smoke and the staff-wielding player reappears while the smaller pig remains beside him (~46158-46170s).

root_causes: Exact-text SQL search for '二姐' fails across all tables (empty results) in several rollouts, forcing reliance on semantic_search recall quality; rollouts that didn't try a broad English-phrased semantic_search over episodes (03) or that drifted to an unrelated later scene sharing the phrase 'second sister' (02, 03) never reached the true clue window.

Even when the correct time window is reached, the disambiguating evidence is a single ~10-second visual transition (large pig dissolves into the player) that must be sampled and correctly read by clip_qa; rollout-01 sampled frames that missed this transition, and rollout-04 sampled the correct frame but misclassified the already-reverted human player as a 'smaller pig demon'.

The judge only sees the final submitted text ('big'/'small'), not the reasoning chain, so a visually-hallucinated answer grounded in the wrong time window (rollout-02, examining an unrelated boss-fight scene) can still score 5 by a 50/50 coincidence, masking a real retrieval failure.
what_worked: Falling back to an English-phrased semantic_search over the episodes table (rather than only CJK literal-text run_sql) successfully surfaced the correct 30-sec chunk even when exact-string search returned nothing.

clip_qa densely sampling frames across the full clue window and specifically catching the dissolve/transformation-back moment (large pig -> red smoke -> player reappears in same spot) gives an unambiguous, directly verifiable signal for size-attribution questions like this one.
transferable_lessons: For CJK proper-noun questions, don't rely solely on exact LIKE-string SQL search on the untranslated term; also run English-phrased semantic_search over episodes, since captions may not literally contain the CJK term the question uses.

For 'which of two similar-looking entities is the player' questions, look specifically for a transformation/reversion transition (a character dissolving/appearing) rather than judging from a single static frame's relative size, since camera perspective and pose can make either figure look larger.

When clip_qa reports seeing content that doesn't match what the retrieval agent's own SQL/episode text says is in that window, treat the clip_qa answer as unreliable and re-verify the time window before trusting it -- a visually confident-sounding clip_qa answer is not proof it examined the right scene.

When the exact-text search on a proper noun/CJK term returns empty across every table, that's a signal to broaden immediately (English paraphrase, broader time range around known related entities) rather than defaulting to a guessed distant time window.
open_questions: Whether rollout-02's clip_qa genuinely saw a pig-demon-like scene at 54300-54450 (perhaps a different, later in-game encounter with two boar-type enemies not captured by the episode captions) or fully hallucinated it was not exhaustively verified with frame-level inspection of that specific rollout's window; only the episode-text mismatch was checked.
